verdicts.reason: A keeps a clean shared left edge and a sensible stack from headline to pills to CTA, but the SOLSTICE wordmark has moved below the headline and grown into a competing focal point, the flavour pills are reversed and their text is tiny, and the bottom margin is tight. B crams the headline, wordmark and subcopy into the top-left with almost no leading, then switches to a centred stack of pills with mismatched sizes (Honey Rosemary is oversized and Blood Orange undersized), which breaks the grid and creates a confused hierarchy against the CTA.
